right.title: Route hydrated landing context to the next household page
right.raw_body: When the landing route reaches hydrated client identity validation, the application SHALL request Home if a member ID is selected, otherwise onboarding. This request SHALL NOT create or validate a member. Existing household page access, member resolution and recovery requirements SHALL continue to apply; a navigation request SHALL NOT guarantee arrival.

### Requirement: Route hydrated landing context to the next household page

This request SHALL NOT create or validate a member. Existing household page access, member resolution and recovery requirements SHALL continue to apply; a navigation request SHALL NOT guarantee arrival.

#### Scenario: Landing client has selected context
- **WHEN** hydrated client identity validation handles the landing route with a selected member ID

left.title: Stage a compatible shared PDF before capture handoff
left.raw_body: For a bounded share POST carrying one nonempty file under files, with a .pdf filename and application/pdf MIME type (case-insensitive) and at most 20,971,520 bytes, transport SHALL commit browser staging before returning 303 to `/capture?share=<token>`. It SHALL NOT render the document or call recipe intake during this handoff.
left.raw_block:
### Requirement: Stage a compatible shared PDF before capture handoff

For a bounded share POST carrying one nonempty file under files, with a .pdf filename and application/pdf MIME type (case-insensitive) and at most 20,971,520 bytes, transport SHALL commit browser staging before returning 303 to `/capture?share=<token>`. It SHALL NOT render the document or call recipe intake during this handoff.

#### Scenario: Compatible transport file committed
- **WHEN** a controlled share POST contains one compatible PDF and staging succeeds
- **THEN** its redirect carries the staged token rather than the file contents
- **AND** no import is created by transport alone

#### Scenario: Document content is unvalidated
- **WHEN** a file meets transport properties but contains corrupt PDF content
- **THEN** transport staging does not certify document readability or successful recipe extraction

right.title: Validate PDF file selection before confirmation
right.raw_body: The ordinary picker SHALL accept a nonempty file of at most 20 MiB (20,971,520 bytes) only when its filename ends in .pdf and its MIME type is application/pdf, without regard to case. Selection validation SHALL check transport properties without parsing the document.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Validate PDF file selection before confirmation

The ordinary picker SHALL accept a nonempty file of at most 20 MiB (20,971,520 bytes) only when its filename ends in .pdf and its MIME type is application/pdf, without regard to case. Selection validation SHALL check transport properties without parsing the document.

#### Scenario: Valid transport properties
- **WHEN** an eligible person selects a nonempty .pdf file with application/pdf type within the byte limit
- **THEN** the client opens PDF confirmation even if the document content has not yet been validated

#### Scenario: Invalid file selection
- **WHEN** a PDF candidate has incompatible extension or MIME type, is empty, or exceeds 20,971,520 bytes
- **THEN** the picker displays a file or size error and does not stage it for PDF confirmation

rationale: Shared PDF transport limits apply separately to browser share staging and ordinary picker validation. Share commits staging and redirects; picker opens confirmation. Neither parses document content or certifies extraction.

left.title: List workflow instances by persisted active status
left.raw_body: GET /api/workflows/active SHALL return 200 with a data array containing only instances whose stored status is Processing or Paused, ordered by descending updatedAt. Each summary SHALL expose id, workflowId, status, createdAt, updatedAt and taskCount.

### Requirement: List workflow instances by persisted active status

GET /api/workflows/active SHALL return 200 with a data array containing only instances whose stored status is Processing or Paused, ordered by descending updatedAt. Each summary SHALL expose id, workflowId, status, createdAt, updatedAt and taskCount.

#### Scenario: Filter stored parent states
- **WHEN** saved instances have Pending, Processing, Paused, Completed and Failed statuses
- **THEN** only Processing and Paused instances appear, newest updatedAt first

#### Scenario: No active instances
- **WHEN** no instance has a selected active status
- **THEN** the response is 200 with an empty data array

#### Scenario: Summary projection
- **WHEN** an active-list read succeeds
- **THEN** each summary exposes its stored identity, workflow name, PascalCase status and timestamps plus the mapped taskCount field without returning task details

right.title: Count stored recipe-import workflows in the import summary
right.raw_body: GET `/api/recipes/import-status` SHALL return unwrapped 200 with importedCount counting Completed recipe-import instances, queueCount counting Pending plus Processing recipe-import instances and failedCount counting Failed recipe-import instances. It SHALL count workflow instances rather than recipes or reports and SHALL exclude other workflow types and Paused instances from these counts.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Count stored recipe-import workflows in the import summary

GET `/api/recipes/import-status` SHALL return unwrapped 200 with importedCount counting Completed recipe-import instances, queueCount counting Pending plus Processing recipe-import instances and failedCount counting Failed recipe-import instances. It SHALL count workflow instances rather than recipes or reports and SHALL exclude other workflow types and Paused instances from these counts.

#### Scenario: Count stored import states
- **WHEN** recipe-import instances exist in Completed, Pending, Processing, Failed and Paused states
- **THEN** the first four contribute to their specified counters and Paused contributes to none

#### Scenario: Other workflow types exist
- **WHEN** url-import or other workflow types have stored states
- **THEN** they contribute to none of these import-summary counters

#### Scenario: No counted instances exist
- **WHEN** no recipe-import instances occupy a counted state
- **THEN** all three counters are zero

rationale: Active workflow listing selects Processing/Paused across workflows; import summary counts Completed/Pending/Processing/Failed recipe-import instances and explicitly excludes Paused. Different endpoints, selections and response shapes; status terms do not imply contradiction.

left.title: Resolve child cron schedules against future UTC minutes
left.raw_body: Child cron scheduling SHALL resolve a whole ${NAME} or ${NAME:-fallback} expression from nonblank configuration then nonblank fallback, and reject missing values. It SHALL parse five numeric cron fields and select the first matching whole UTC minute strictly after the supplied clock instant, searching no further than five years from its initial cursor.
left.raw_block:
### Requirement: Resolve child cron schedules against future UTC minutes

Child cron scheduling SHALL resolve a whole ${NAME} or ${NAME:-fallback} expression from nonblank configuration then nonblank fallback, and reject missing values. It SHALL parse five numeric cron fields and select the first matching whole UTC minute strictly after the supplied clock instant, searching no further than five years from its initial cursor.

#### Scenario: Configured expression
- **WHEN** the cron text is a whole configuration expression with a nonblank configured value
- **THEN** the trimmed configured value is used before any fallback

#### Scenario: Fallback or missing configuration
- **WHEN** the whole configuration expression has no nonblank configured value
- **THEN** a nonblank fallback is used, otherwise scheduling throws

#### Scenario: Next matching minute
- **WHEN** a valid cron matches the current minute and a later minute
- **THEN** the search begins at the next whole UTC minute and selects the first later match

#### Scenario: Numeric cron fields
- **WHEN** a valid expression uses comma lists, ascending ranges, wildcards or positive slash steps in minute, hour, day-of-month, month and day-of-week fields
- **THEN** all five fields must match; day-of-week 0 and 7 both identify Sunday

#### Scenario: Invalid or impossible schedule
- **WHEN** an expression has invalid fields or has no matching minute within the search horizon
- **THEN** scheduling throws before child acceptance; no guaranteed recurring workflow is created

right.title: Default the automatic restore schedule to daily UTC
right.raw_body: Blank or absent DEMO_RESTORE_CRON_UTC SHALL select 0 3 * * *. Nonblank configuration SHALL supply the restore cron. Scheduling SHALL follow background-processing requirement `Resolve child cron schedules against future UTC minutes`, using a future whole UTC minute rather than an immediate catch-up run.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Default the automatic restore schedule to daily UTC

Blank or absent DEMO_RESTORE_CRON_UTC SHALL select 0 3 * * *. Nonblank configuration SHALL supply the restore cron. Scheduling SHALL follow background-processing requirement `Resolve child cron schedules against future UTC minutes`, using a future whole UTC minute rather than an immediate catch-up run.

#### Scenario: Before daily target
- **WHEN** the default cron is resolved at 02:30 UTC
- **THEN** the next restore root schedule is 03:00 UTC that day

#### Scenario: At daily target
- **WHEN** the default cron is resolved at exactly 03:00 UTC
- **THEN** the next restore root schedule is 03:00 UTC the following day

#### Scenario: Custom daily target
- **WHEN** a valid configured cron selects 04:30 UTC and the clock is before that target
- **THEN** that configured target supplies the next eligible UTC schedule

rationale: Demo restoration supplies default or configured cron; background-processing owns parsing and strictly future UTC-minute selection. At-target scenario agrees with the generic next-minute rule.

#### Scenario: Save pending
- **WHEN** a single-page changed instruction save is still pending
- **THEN** Save and Cancel are disabled and another row editor cannot be opened

#### Scenario: Save rejects
- **WHEN** a single-page instruction update rejects
- **THEN** the draft stays open with an error alert and Try again can resubmit it

right.title: Retain editing and offer another attempt after detail Save failure
right.raw_body: When the detail-field update request rejects while the sheet remains open, the editor SHALL remain open with its current drafts and display “Could not save changes. Try again.” Saving SHALL end and Save and Cancel SHALL become available subject to local Save eligibility. Starting another Save SHALL clear the prior error. Failure feedback SHALL NOT assert that stored data is unchanged.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Retain editing and offer another attempt after detail Save failure

Try again.” Saving SHALL end and Save and Cancel SHALL become available subject to local Save eligibility. Starting another Save SHALL clear the prior error. left.title: Accept ordinary management requests through household access
left.raw_body: Management operations SHALL apply the household-identity requirement “Authenticate protected API requests independently”. Successful ordinary workflow acceptance SHALL return HTTP 202 with a flat message and taskId identifying the accepted workflow instance.

#### Scenario: Restore acceptance

right.title: Accept demo snapshot capture as background work
right.raw_body: An authenticated POST /api/management/demo-capture with demo mode disabled SHALL trigger demo-capture with empty parameters and return 202 containing message Demo capture task enqueued. and taskId identifying the accepted workflow instance. Acceptance SHALL follow background-processing requirement `Persist initial workflow and task identities before returning` and SHALL NOT certify completion.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Accept demo snapshot capture as background work
An authenticated POST /api/management/demo-capture with demo mode disabled SHALL trigger demo-capture with empty parameters and return 202 containing message Demo capture task enqueued. and taskId identifying the accepted workflow instance. Acceptance SHALL follow background-processing requirement `Persist initial workflow and task identities before returning` and SHALL NOT certify completion.

#### Scenario: Capture accepted
- **WHEN** demo mode is disabled and authenticated workflow acceptance succeeds for demo-capture
- **THEN** 202 contains the enqueue message and accepted instance identity as taskId

#### Scenario: Capture outside automatic mode
- **WHEN** an authorized operator requests demo-capture with DEMO_MODE disabled and workflow acceptance succeeds
- **THEN** the management action still accepts capture; automatic demo activation is not an action-level prerequisite

#### Scenario: Capture rejected in demo mode
- **WHEN** demo mode is enabled and capture is requested through management, a generic workflow trigger or task reset, or previously accepted capture work reaches execution
- **THEN** capture SHALL be rejected at that boundary

rationale: Ordinary backup/restore/disaster-recovery acceptance and demo snapshot capture invoke different workflows/endpoints. Demo capture explicitly has a mode guard; ordinary 202 envelope similarity establishes shared background acceptance convention only.

left.title: Project the latest selected management result
left.raw_body: When the latest selected management instance is an ordinary management workflow, GET /api/management/status SHALL return its instance identity as workflowId, workflowType, status, createdAt and updatedAt, with the most recently updated completed task result that is non-null, or a null result.

When the latest selected management instance is an ordinary management workflow, GET /api/management/status SHALL return its instance identity as workflowId, workflowType, status, createdAt and updatedAt, with the most recently updated completed task result that is non-null, or a null result.

#### Scenario: Completed result
- **WHEN** the selected ordinary instance has multiple completed tasks with non-null results
- **THEN** the response result comes from the most recently updated such task

#### Scenario: No completed result

- **THEN** the response result is null

right.title: Read latest management workflow diagnostics
right.raw_body: GET /api/management/status SHALL select the newest created instance among db-backup, db-restore, db-disaster-recovery, demo-capture and demo-restore. When found, it SHALL return its identity, workflow type, persisted status and timestamps, plus the newest updated completed-task result with a nonnull stored result, if present.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Read latest management workflow diagnostics

GET /api/management/status SHALL select the newest created instance among db-backup, db-restore, db-disaster-recovery, demo-capture and demo-restore. When found, it SHALL return its identity, workflow type, persisted status and timestamps, plus the newest updated completed-task result with a nonnull stored result, if present.

#### Scenario: Latest management selection
- **WHEN** several selected management workflows exist and status is read successfully
- **THEN** the newest by createdAt is returned even if it differs from the caller's earlier taskId

#### Scenario: Completed task result
- **WHEN** the selected instance has completed tasks with stored results
- **THEN** result is taken from the newest updated such task, which can be reschedule rather than restore

rationale: Same GET status endpoint/result projection overlaps for ordinary workflows; demo requirement additionally owns selection across ordinary and demo types. Outcomes agree, but projection authority is not named. Request owner clarification before any consolidation; no contradiction proven.

left.title: Rebuild lexical search content during compatible restore
left.raw_body: For a sidecar with the current schema version, restore SHALL rebuild lexical text, metadata and source fingerprint from restored recipe facts and upsert the search document with ready lexical index status. It SHALL not rehydrate the sidecar’s lexical text or metadata.
left.raw_block:
### Requirement: Rebuild lexical search content during compatible restore

For a sidecar with the current schema version, restore SHALL rebuild lexical text, metadata and source fingerprint from restored recipe facts and upsert the search document with ready lexical index status. It SHALL not rehydrate the sidecar’s lexical text or metadata.

#### Scenario: Compatible sidecar
- **WHEN** a readable sidecar has the current schema
- **THEN** restore writes ready lexical content built from the restored recipe

#### Scenario: Legacy terms
- **WHEN** a current-schema sidecar contains obsolete dietary text or metadata
- **THEN** restore replaces that content with the current recipe-derived projection

right.title: Publish lexical content before optional embedding work
right.raw_body: Indexing eligible content SHALL persist canonical text, metadata, schema version, source fingerprint, lexical ready status and indexing time before generating an embedding. With no embedding provider it SHALL leave embedding status pending while preserving published lexical content.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Publish lexical content before optional embedding work

Indexing eligible content SHALL persist canonical text, metadata, schema version, source fingerprint, lexical ready status and indexing time before generating an embedding. With no embedding provider it SHALL leave embedding status pending while preserving published lexical content.

#### Scenario: Provider unavailable
- **WHEN** lexical publication succeeds and no embedding provider is supplied
- **THEN** the document remains lexical-ready with embedding pending

#### Scenario: Embedding succeeds
- **WHEN** the provider returns a nonempty vector and the stored source fingerprint still matches
- **THEN** indexing persists the vector with its model, matching embedding fingerprint and ready embedding status

rationale: Restore with compatible sidecar rebuilds from restored facts; ordinary indexing publishes before optional embedding. Different triggers and guarantees; search-indexing explicitly links restore ownership.

left.title: Seed an initial restore only for eligible demo startup
left.raw_body: On hosted startup with demo enabled, the seeder SHALL schedule demo-restore only when no demo-restore instance is Pending or Processing. Disabled demo mode SHALL skip seeding. The eligible startup SHALL use empty parameters and the next configured UTC cron occurrence as its root-task schedule.
left.raw_block:
### Requirement: Seed an initial restore only for eligible demo startup

On hosted startup with demo enabled, the seeder SHALL schedule demo-restore only when no demo-restore instance is Pending or Processing. Disabled demo mode SHALL skip seeding. The eligible startup SHALL use empty parameters and the next configured UTC cron occurrence as its root-task schedule.

#### Scenario: Disabled startup
- **WHEN** demo mode is disabled when seeding starts
- **THEN** no demo restore is seeded

#### Scenario: Existing active restore
- **WHEN** a demo-restore instance is Pending or Processing
- **THEN** seeding returns without creating another initial restore

#### Scenario: Eligible startup
- **WHEN** demo mode is enabled with no Pending or Processing demo-restore and cron calculation and acceptance succeed
- **THEN** a demo-restore instance is accepted with its root scheduled at the next configured UTC occurrence

#### Scenario: Only paused history
- **WHEN** only Paused or terminal demo-restore instances exist and other prerequisites succeed
- **THEN** those instances do not suppress the initial seed

right.title: Seed the maintenance schedule when no active instance exists
right.raw_body: At startup, maintenance seeding SHALL skip when a dreaming instance is Pending or Processing. Otherwise it SHALL request dreaming at the next configured DREAMING_CRON_UTC occurrence, defaulting to 06:00 UTC daily through the shared background-processing cron rules.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Seed the maintenance schedule when no active instance exists

At startup, maintenance seeding SHALL skip when a dreaming instance is Pending or Processing. Otherwise it SHALL request dreaming at the next configured DREAMING_CRON_UTC occurrence, defaulting to 06:00 UTC daily through the shared background-processing cron rules.

#### Scenario: No active maintenance
- **WHEN** startup seeding finds no Pending or Processing dreaming instance
- **THEN** it requests the next configured maintenance occurrence

#### Scenario: Active maintenance
- **WHEN** startup seeding finds a Pending dreaming instance
- **THEN** it does not seed another instance

#### Scenario: Seed failure
- **WHEN** the hosted seeding attempt throws
- **THEN** the failure is logged by the hosted startup boundary

rationale: Separate startup seeders guard separate workflow IDs: demo-restore versus dreaming. Both avoid duplicate Pending/Processing seeds, but demo has enabled-mode predicate and different cron. Paused history scenario is consistent with both guards.

- **WHEN** a member opens the grocery view for any future week while current-week Toilet paper remains unchecked
- **THEN** next week's supper groceries and the editable Toilet paper extra appear together without creating a next-week Toilet paper occurrence

- **THEN** the action targets the current occurrence and preserves all earlier snapshots

#### Scenario: No additional week label
- **WHEN** a current outstanding extra is presented with future-week groceries
- **THEN** it uses the ordinary compact `Extra` source label without `This week` or another week-origin label

right.title: Apply received extras only to eligible shopping views
right.raw_body: A parsed `grocery_extras_updated` event SHALL identify the occurrences' absolute Monday. It SHALL reconcile those rows when the grocery view displays that Monday or any later Monday and the occurrences belong to the deployment current week. Each future-week view SHALL retain only unchecked extras. Other views, absent identity, or unusable collections SHALL trigger no guessed update.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Apply received extras only to eligible shopping views

A parsed `grocery_extras_updated` event SHALL identify the occurrences' absolute Monday. It SHALL reconcile those rows when the grocery view displays that Monday or any later Monday and the occurrences belong to the deployment current week. Each future-week view SHALL retain only unchecked extras. Other views, absent identity, or unusable collections SHALL trigger no guessed update.

#### Scenario: Matching loaded week
- **WHEN** an extra update identifies the loaded absolute Monday with a valid authoritative collection
- **THEN** loaded extra rows are replaced while recipe-derived rows and checks remain unchanged

#### Scenario: Future-week shopping view
- **WHEN** an extra update identifies the deployment current Monday while any future week is displayed
- **THEN** that view reconciles its projected extras by identity and version, removes checked or removed extras, and preserves next week's recipe-derived rows

#### Scenario: Another week
- **WHEN** an extra update identifies a Monday not eligible for the displayed current or future-week shopping view
- **THEN** the displayed grocery rows remain unchanged through that handler

#### Scenario: Week identity is absent
- **WHEN** an extra update omits its absolute Monday
- **THEN** the client requests authoritative state rather than applying the collection to the displayed offset

rationale: Shopping owns projected unchecked current-week extras in future-week views and edit targets; live-updates owns receiving eligible absolute-week collections. Same inclusion policy is intentionally reflected in read presentation and received reconciliation.

- **THEN** the application redirects to Welcome and requests deletion of the access cookie

right.title: Apply member context after household access

Subsequent member resolution SHALL follow the existing household-identity requirements.

- **THEN** the application redirects to onboarding

right.title: Close atomically with retry-safe round ownership
right.raw_body: Close SHALL capture the intended round and persisted plan, commit its aggregate snapshot and lock, and clear that round once as one durable outcome. A failed persistence boundary SHALL leave the round votes available. A retry after committed close SHALL return or recover that outcome without clearing later votes.
right.raw_block:
### Requirement: Close atomically with retry-safe round ownership

Close SHALL capture the intended round and persisted plan, commit its aggregate snapshot and lock, and clear that round once as one durable outcome. A failed persistence boundary SHALL leave the round votes available. A retry after committed close SHALL return or recover that outcome without clearing later votes.

#### Scenario: Snapshot failure
- **WHEN** snapshot persistence fails before close commit
- **THEN** no lock/history/clear partial outcome is committed; votes can be retried

#### Scenario: Lost response
- **WHEN** close commits but its response is lost; early votes arrive and the same close is retried
- **THEN** the retry recognizes completion and preserves every later vote

#### Scenario: Publication failure
- **WHEN** close commits but SSE publication fails
- **THEN** durable state remains closed; retry/reload can recover it without duplicate history or clearing

#### Scenario: Late vote
- **WHEN** a vote races the serialized close boundary
- **THEN** it is included in the closed snapshot and cleared, or retained as a next-round vote, never silently lost

#### Scenario: Concurrent closes
- **WHEN** two closes target the same round
- **THEN** one durable close outcome is produced; neither can replace history with an empty retry

#### Scenario: Reopen versus stale close
- **WHEN** a closed week reopens and a stale close request from the prior round arrives
- **THEN** the stale request cannot close or clear the new round

#### Scenario: Pending browser suggestion
- **WHEN** a displayed suggestion has not been persisted when close takes its plan snapshot
- **THEN** it is not selected in history; browser promotion remains its existing separate operation
